title: About me
goal: Say who you are, where you're from, where you live and which languages you speak, and ask others the same.
intro:
In this unit you'll learn the personal pronouns, the present tense of 'to be' in full, and the basic question words. With these you can introduce yourself and ask the questions every Pashtun will ask you: What's your name? Where are you from? Do you speak Pashto?

Good news: Pashto doesn't move words around to make a question. You just put the question word where the answer would go.

vocab.note: Same spelling for he and she; the verb shows the gender (دی / ده).
Comes before the owner: د احمد کور 'Ahmad's house'.

vocab.en: from (with نه / څخه after the noun)
vocab.note: له کابل نه la kābúl na 'from Kabul'.
m. f. پښتنه paṣtə́na; pl پښتانه paṣtānə́.
f. An Englishman is انګرېز angréz.
f. Also: دري darí (Afghan Persian), عربي ʿarabí (Arabic).
Present stem وای-: وايم wā́yəm 'I say'. پښتو وايم 'I speak Pashto'.
Present: زده کوم zdə kawə́m 'I learn / am learning'.
Comes after the word it refers to: زه هم 'me too'.

phrases.en: Where are you from? (lit. you are of which place?)

phrases.native: زه له انګلستان نه راغلی يم.
phrases.roman: zə la inglistā́n na rāġə́lay yəm.

phrases.en: Yes, I speak a little Pashto.

phrases.native: ستاسو په ليدو ډېر خوشاله شوم.
phrases.roman: stāso pə lidó ḍer xoshā́la shwəm.
phrases.en: I'm very glad to meet you.

grammar.title: Pronouns and 'to be'
grammar.body:
The subject pronouns and the present of 'to be' (the copula) go together:

زه يم zə yəm — I am
ته يې tə ye — you are (informal)
هغه دی haġá day — he is
هغه ده haġá da — she is
موږ يو muẓ yu — we are
تاسو ياست tāso yāst — you are (polite/plural) (Peshawar/eastern speech: يئ yəy)
هغوی دي haġwí di — they are

Notice that **هغه** means both 'he' and 'she' — only the verb tells you which: دی for a man or masculine thing, ده for a woman or feminine thing. **دا** (this) works the same way: دا احمد دی / دا زرمينه ده.

Pashto often drops the pronoun, because the verb ending already shows the person: ښه يم 'I'm fine', چېرته يې؟ 'where are you?'.

grammar.title: Question words stay in place
grammar.body:
To ask a question in Pashto, put the question word **where the answer would go** — usually just before the verb — and keep the normal word order. 'Your name is Ahmad' → 'Your name is *what*?': ستاسو نوم احمد دی → ستاسو نوم **څه** دی؟

The key question words: **څه** tsə what · **څوک** tsok who · **چېرته** chérta where · **کوم** kum which · **څنګه** tsə́nga how. Yes/no questions have no special word at all — just raise your voice at the end: ته پښتون يې؟ 'Are you a Pashtun?'

dialogue.title: At a wedding in Peshawar
dialogue.setting: Emma, a foreign aid worker learning Pashto, is seated next to Palwasha at a family wedding.

lines.speaker: Palwasha
lines.native: السلام عليکم. ستاسو نوم څه دی؟
lines.roman: assalā́mu ʿaláykum. stāso num tsə day?

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.native: وعليکم السلام. زما نوم ايما دی. ستاسو نوم څه دی؟
lines.roman: wa ʿaláykum assalā́m. zmā num émā day. stāso num tsə day?
lines.en: Hello. My name is Emma. What's your name?

lines.speaker: Palwasha
lines.native: زما نوم پلوشه ده. ماشاالله، تاسو پښتو وايئ!
lines.roman: zmā num palwáṣa da. māshāllā́h, tāso paṣtó wā́yəy!
lines.en: My name is Palwasha. Wow, you speak Pashto!

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.native: لږ لږ. زه پښتو زده کوم.
lines.roman: ləẓ ləẓ. zə paṣtó zdə kawə́m.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.native: زه له انګلستان نه يم، خو اوس په پېښور کې اوسېږم.
lines.roman: zə la inglistā́n na yəm, xo os pə peṣawár ke oséẓəm.
lines.en: I'm from England, but now I live in Peshawar.

lines.speaker: Palwasha
lines.native: ښه! زه هم په پېښور کې اوسېږم.
lines.roman: ṣə! zə ham pə peṣawár ke oséẓəm.
lines.en: Great! I live in Peshawar too.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.native: بښنه غواړم، مهرباني وکړئ ورو خبرې وکړئ.
lines.roman: baṣə́na ġwā́ṛəm, mehrabāní wə́kṛəy wro xabə́re wə́kṛəy.

lines.speaker: Palwasha
lines.native: سمه ده. تاسو په انګرېزي، اردو او پښتو پوهېږئ؟
lines.roman: sáma da. tāso pə angrezí, urdú aw paṣtó pohéẓəy?
lines.en: OK. Do you understand English, Urdu and Pashto?

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.native: انګرېزي هو، اردو لږ، پښتو ورو ورو.
lines.roman: angrezí ho, urdú ləẓ, paṣtó wro wro.
lines.en: English yes, Urdu a little, Pashto slowly but surely.

lines.speaker: Palwasha
lines.native: ستاسو په ليدو ډېره خوشاله شوم!
lines.roman: stāso pə lidó ḍéra xoshā́la shwəm!
lines.en: I'm very glad to meet you!

culture: Pashto is spoken on both sides of the Durand Line, the Afghanistan–Pakistan border, and people will often ask *which* Pashto you are learning: the Kandahari 'Pashto' of the south or the Peshawari 'Pakhto' of the north. Both are welcome — Pashtuns are delighted when a foreigner tries their language, and even a few sentences will win you smiles and tea. The word پښتو also means the Pashtun code of honour (*Pashtunwali*): saying of someone that he 'has Pashto' means he behaves honourably, keeps his word and looks after his guests.

tip.title: Pronouns and 'to be'
tip.body:
- زه **يم** · ته **يې** · هغه **دی** (he) / هغه **ده** (she) · موږ **يو** · تاسو **ياست** · هغوی **دي**.
- **هغه** is both 'he' and 'she': only دی or ده tells you which.
- **هم** 'too' comes after its word: زه هم 'me too'.
tip.pattern: هغه پښتون دی  ·  موږ ښه يو

sentences.native: دا احمد دی او هغه پلوشه ده.
sentences.roman: dā ahmád day aw haġá palwáṣa da.
sentences.en: This is Ahmad and that's Palwasha.

tip.title: Question words stay in place
tip.body:
- Put the question word where the answer would go, just before the verb: ستا نوم احمد دی → ستا نوم **څه** دی؟
- **څه** what · **څوک** who · **څنګه** how.
- A yes/no question needs no extra word: just raise your voice at the end.

sentences.native: ستاسو نوم څه دی، حاجي صاحب؟
sentences.roman: stāso num tsə day, hājí sāhíb?

lessons.title: Saying where you are from

tip.title: 'From': د … or له … نه
tip.body:
- **د** + place + verb says where you belong: زه **د** کابل يم 'I'm from Kabul'.
- **له** … **نه** wraps the place for 'from' a starting point: **له** کندهار **نه** راغلی يم 'I've come from Kandahar'.
- Ask with **کوم** 'which' or **چېرته** 'where': د کوم ځای يې؟
tip.pattern: زه د + place + يم  ·  له + place + نه

new: زه له انګلستان نه راغلی يم.

sentences.native: هغه له کندهار نه راغلی دی.
sentences.roman: haġá la kandahā́r na rāġə́lay day.

lessons.title: Where do you live?

tip.title: Present tense endings
tip.body:
- Most present verbs take these endings: زه **-əm** · ته **-e** · هغه / هغوی **-i** · موږ **-u** · تاسو **-əy**.
- اوسېږم oséẓəm 'I live', اوسېږې, اوسېږي, اوسېږو, اوسېږئ.
- 'In a city' is **په** … **کې**: په کابل کې.

new: ستاسو په ليدو ډېر خوشاله شوم.

sentences.native: هغه په کوم ښار کې اوسېږي؟
sentences.roman: haġá pə kum ṣār ke oséẓi?
sentences.en: Which city does he live in?

sentences.native: موږ اوس په پېښور کې اوسېږو.
sentences.roman: muẓ os pə peṣawár ke oséẓu.

sentences.en: Kabul is a very nice city.

sentences.native: ته هم په پېښور کې اوسېږې؟
sentences.roman: tə ham pə peṣawár ke oséẓe?
sentences.en: Do you live in Peshawar too?

sentences.native: زه هم ستاسو په ليدو ډېر خوشاله شوم.
sentences.roman: zə ham stāso pə lidó ḍer xoshā́la shwəm.
sentences.en: I'm very glad to meet you too.

tip.title: Speaking and understanding a language
tip.body:
- 'I speak Pashto' is **پښتو وايم** (lit. I say Pashto) — the language comes before the verb.
- 'Understand' takes **په**: **په** پښتو پوهېږم 'I understand Pashto'.
- Same endings as before: وايم، وايې، وايي، وايو، وايئ.

sentences.en: Yes, I understand Pashto a little.

tip.title: زده کول — to learn
tip.body:
- Many verbs are a word + **کول** 'to do': زده کول 'to learn' (lit. do learning).
- Only کول changes: زده **کوم** · زده **کوې** · زده **کوي** · زده **کوو** · زده **کوئ**.
- To slow someone down: ورو خبرې وکړئ 'speak slowly'; to a friend بيا ووايه 'say it again'.

sentences.native: احمد جان، بيا ووايه، پوه نه شوم.
sentences.roman: ahmád jān, biyā́ wə́wāya, poh na shwəm.
sentences.en: Ahmad dear, say it again — I didn't understand.
I'm learning Pashto bit by bit.
